body:
I suspect that's a consequence of how audio works on Windows. Godot uses WASAPI in shared mode, in which audio formats and settings including buffer size are mostly dictated by the audio driver and Windows settings. As such, you can query the latency the operating system uses, but you cannot change it. That's what _"Audio output latency may be constrained by the host operating system and audio hardware drivers."_ in the documentation refers to.

The code comment here
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/efb40c1524e54f2cf52f213e248bd0a7b790975a/drivers/wasapi/audio_driver_wasapi.cpp#L416-L416
_may_ be outdated starting from Windows 10 (I didn't test this and am only going by the WASAPI docs), but even then, 10 ms would be the maximum buffer size and you could only get shorter latencies, not longer ones.

Sidenote: Reddit is full of threads about Creative pushing broken drivers for X4. I had no crackling/popping when using the default headphone jack on my computer, so it seems to be my setup rather than godot that causes the real issue.

> The code comment here
> 
>  // Due to WASAPI Shared Mode we have no control of the buffer size 
> 
> _may_ be outdated starting from Windows 10.

Ah, correction: There are actually two code paths, one using `IAudioClient` and one using `IAudioClient3` (which will presumably be taken on Windows 10). The `IAudioClient3` variant actively tries to set the requested output latency, but on my machine, Godot works with these constraints:
```
WASAPI: Activated output_device using IAudioClient3 interface
WASAPI: nSamplesPerSec = 48000
WASAPI: fundamental_period_frames = 480
WASAPI: min_period_frames = 480
WASAPI: max_period_frames = 480
WASAPI: selected a period frame size of 480
WASAPI: audio buffer frames: 480 calculated latency: 10ms
```
So it's essentially "you can pick any output latency you want as long as it is 10 ms." The values may be different for your USB sound card, but apparently, 50 ms is not in the allowed range there either.

You can check these values for your devices by enabling "Verbose stdout" in the project settings under Debug/Settings.
